evidence.claim: The fetch captures the store generation before it suspends and passes that stale reading to insert when it resumes; it returns the fetched value to its caller regardless of whether the insert succeeded.
evidence.verification: Source analysis. Read Fetcher.fetch top to bottom and note the order of the four statements: generation read (19), suspension point (20), origin call (21), insert with the captured value (22), return of value (23). The boolean returned by insert is not bound at line 22.

result.observed: observed_generation is read at line 19, strictly before the yield at line 20; insert receives it at line 22; line 23 returns value unconditionally.
result.interpretation: Any generation change occurring during the suspension is invisible to the fetch but fatal to its insert, and the caller cannot tell the difference.

evidence.claim: Store.insert writes nothing when the supplied generation differs from the current generation, and records the rejection.
evidence.verification: Source analysis. The guard at line 29 compares the argument with self._generation; lines 30-31 increment rejected_inserts and return False; the assignment at line 32 is reachable only on an exact match.

result.observed: Inequality short-circuits before any mutation of self._entries.
result.interpretation: Insert rejection is the only mechanism in this function that can cause a key to be absent after a completed fetch; it is distinguishable from eviction by the rejected_inserts counter.

evidence.claim: Store.invalidate increments the generation unconditionally, independently of the prefix and of whether any entry matched.
evidence.verification: Source analysis. The increment at line 40 sits outside the deletion loop at lines 38-39, is not guarded by the contents of doomed, and does not reference prefix. The counter is a single store-wide integer initialised at store.py:12, not a per-prefix or per-key structure.

result.observed: self._generation += 1 executes on every call, including calls that delete zero entries.
result.interpretation: The generation is a global epoch, so invalidating one key space invalidates in-flight work in all key spaces. This is the fact that makes the prefix irrelevant to the outcome.

evidence.claim: In the instruction's interleaving the outcome is the same for an unrelated prefix and a matching prefix: zero entries dropped, generation 0 to 1, the value returned to the caller, no entry in the store, and one rejected insert.
evidence.verification: PYTHONPATH=environment/src python3 reference/reproductions/repro_unrelated_prefix.py — run from the task root with the pinned source, Python 3.12, no network. The Scheduler fixes the interleaving explicitly, so the result carries no timing dependence.

result.observed: Both prefixes print entries_dropped_by_invalidate: 0, generation_before: 0, generation_after: 1, value_returned_to_caller: 'value-for-user:42', value_in_cache_afterwards: None, rejected_inserts: 1.
result.interpretation: Identical output across the two prefixes rules out the prefix-matters explanation. rejected_inserts: 1 alongside entries_dropped: 0 rules out eviction and identifies the generation guard as the mechanism.
